transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-10 16:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Rivera (Redwood SE), Jordan Price (Glacier CTO), Priya Singh (Lead Eng), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Sana Ahmed (Product)

Summary (auto): quick SDK walkthrough, auth options, env setup, plan POC.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick round of intros?
00:08 Jordan Price: Jordan here, CTO at Glacier Retail, focused on in-store search and recommendation latency, curious about cost math.
00:15 Priya Singh: Priya, lead on integration, we'll be running a small pilot across 10 stores first.
00:22 Liam O'Connor: Liam, infra, i'll handle network and account access.
00:28 Alex Chen: Great; maya will run the SDK demo. maya you want to intro?
00:33 Maya Rivera: yeah hi all, maya redwood SE. we'll do python then typescript quickstarts, auth, and a bit about streaming and batching. i'll also show the console quickstart. quick note, transcript may have small errors, apologies.
01:02 Maya Rivera: first, pip install redwood-sdk, or npm i @redwood/inference-sdk, set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY or use our client with SSO token for Dedicated/Private.
01:22 Priya Singh: quick q - we want KMS so keys never land in plain envs. how does that play with client?
01:30 Maya Rivera: you can use env var that points to a short-lived token minted by your KMS workflow, or we support OIDC/SAML on Dedicated so tokens are exchanged without long lived keys in app env. for quickstarts we use REDWOOD_API_KEY but for POC we'll recommend a short lived auth flow.
02:05 Jordan Price: and audit logs? we need per-request traceability for PCI scope.
02:12 Maya Rivera: console captures request traces; on Dedicated/Private you get full audit logs with timestamp, token id, route, model version. we'll share SOC2 and logging docs after.
03:00 Maya Rivera: moving to python demo, copy/paste from quickstart:
03:08 Maya Rivera: "from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(prompt="store product search", model="redwood-ax-13b")
print(resp.text)"
03:35 Priya Singh: that model name might be misheard — is it Redwood-AX? we vendor a lot of model names internally. is there a catalog call?
03:42 Maya Rivera: yes we have catalog endpoints and the console list. model names can change, we provide pinned versions for POCs. we'll include the catalog link.
04:10 Liam O'Connor: what about streaming tokens to the client? for chat UI we need immediate partials.
04:17 Maya Rivera: we support streaming via websockets or server-sent events in both SDKs; typescript example:
04:24 Maya Rivera: "const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.streamGenerate({ prompt })
stream.on('data', chunk => { /* append to UI */ })
"
04:50 Jordan Price: and for error handling? backoff? what if a node drops?
04:56 Maya Rivera: SDK has retry/backoff built-in and the runtime does automatic fallback to compatible model variants if you're on Hosted and capacity issues. for Dedicated we surface capacity metrics in console; we'll show autoscale controls in a sec.
05:28 Alex Chen: quick qualification — what's your expected qps and latency budget?
05:33 Jordan Price: aiming for 150 qps across 10 stores at peak, p95 under 300ms for short queries. token lengths small ~40 tokens typical.
05:45 Maya Rivera: ok that helps. latency SLOs depend on model size and quantization; for 13B quantized models on A100 you'd be around 100-200ms p95, but it varies. we'll send our perf spreadsheet.
06:10 Priya Singh: can we run a baseline on our logs? we have historical query traces.
06:17 Maya Rivera: yes we'll ingest a sample prompt set — POC plan is to run your traces for a week against a pinned model to measure latency/cost.
06:30 Alex Chen: auth again — we typically push secrets into AWS Secrets Manager and want short lived creds. is there a recommended flow?
06:36 Maya Rivera: recommended is to have a small auth service that exchanges an OIDC token for a Redwood session token; for Dedicated/Private you can configure SSO and our agent will accept assertions. we'll include an example in the repo.
07:05 Priya Singh: network egress — data residency: can we keep traffic inside our VPC for Private?
07:11 Maya Rivera: for Private yes fully in your VPC/on-prem. Dedicated offers VPC peering options and private endpoints. Hosted goes over TLS to our endpoints — if you need egress controls we suggest Dedicated.
07:45 Liam O'Connor: for the POC we'd like to start Hosted to iterate quickly then switch to Dedicated if latency/cost needs it. is migration seamless?
07:53 Maya Rivera: yes same APIs, you can pin model versions and change routing policy. console helps you switch traffic gradually with canaries.
08:20 Jordan Price: show me the quick typescript example for typing results and validations.
08:27 Maya Rivera: types are small: "type GenerateResponse = { text: string; tokens: number }" and SDK returns typed promises in TS, with streaming event types. we'll paste code in the follow-up.
09:00 Maya Rivera: also quick note on caching: prefix caching and KV cache for short-lived session use can cut token cost a lot — console shows hit rates.
09:20 Priya Singh: do you do on-the-fly quantization? we run 8-bit to save cost.
09:26 Maya Rivera: runtime supports int8 and dynamic quantization; Optimize tool suggests profiles per workload. we'll include suggested quant profiles for retail.
10:00 Alex Chen: demo the console quickly?
10:05 Maya Rivera: sure, sharing screen (described): navigation: model catalog, route configs, observability tab with token-level breakdown, rolling updates section. you can set autoscale policies and configure burst capacity.
11:00 Priya Singh: can we set different policies per route? e.g., search vs recommendations.
11:05 Maya Rivera: yes per-route overrides — different batching windows, priorities, and fallbacks. good for separating critical search from cheap recommendations.
11:40 Jordan Price: SLA questions — what uptime do you guarantee and what's escalation?
11:48 Alex Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime; Hosted has uptime targets in our terms. for enterprise packaging we'll include contact and incident escalation process.
12:10 Maya Rivera: back to SDK — installation and env setup: python v3.10+, pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY or pass client param. TS: node 18+, npm i @redwood/inference-sdk, set env or pass apiKey. example commit links will be in follow up.
13:00 Priya Singh: any gotchas with serverless? we use lambda for certain endpoints.
13:06 Maya Rivera: we recommend using a warm connection or batching gateway for lambda to avoid cold start tokenization overhead; Optimize can suggest batching settings.
13:45 Liam O'Connor: what about cost — per-token pricing and reserved capacity?
13:52 Alex Chen: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity monthly. for your qps we can run a cost estimate once we have trace sample; we'll include a preliminary estimate in the perf sheet.
14:20 Jordan Price: will we need data deletion / retention controls for PCI?
14:25 Maya Rivera: yes retention policies configurable; on Dedicated/Private you control retention and can disable logging. Hosted has retention options and we can offer contract terms for shorter retention windows.
15:00 Alex Chen: ok let's sketch the POC: 1) share quickstart + repo, 2) Glacier shares sample logs, 3) Redwood runs baseline in Hosted for 1 week, 4) compare latency/cost, 5) decide Dedicated. schedule Jan 19-26.
15:25 Priya Singh: sounds good. can you include benchmark scripts?
15:30 Maya Rivera: yes we'll include load scripts and a runner that replays prompts preserving timing distribution.
16:00 Jordan Price: one more on security — SAML SSO for console? our SOC requires SAML plus RBAC.
16:07 Alex Chen: yes we support SAML/SSO and granular RBAC for console plus audit logs. we'll include a diagram in the follow up.
16:40 Sana Ahmed: product question: does Optimize give recommendations automatically or you run eval sets?
16:45 Maya Rivera: Optimize has both automated suggestions based on traffic patterns and manual eval runs against your prompt sets. we can run regressions and tie alerts to prompt sets.
17:20 Jordan Price: ok great. any blockers for us to start? infra access to a test account and a contract?
17:27 Alex Chen: contract can be minimal for a POC; we'll coordinate with sales operations. infra access is main blocker, liam can share.
17:40 Liam O'Connor: i'll create an IAM role and share cross-account access by Friday.
17:48 Alex Chen: perfect. we'll follow up with links and the perf spreadsheet.
18:05 Maya Rivera: closing demo, i'll send the repo and a README with setup steps: export REDWOOD_API_KEY, pip/npm install, run sample server, run replay tool.
18:25 Jordan Price: thanks everyone, good runthrough.
18:30 Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll be in touch and send materials by Tue.

Auto-generated action items (transcript): Alex - send quickstarts & pricing; Maya - share perf sheet & benchmark scripts; Priya - provision test account.

End of transcript.
